note: What the three of them say when somebody clicks on them. Lifted out of the pane so the page stops paying for them and so the pool can grow without a ceiling. Regenerate and replace this file alone to change what they say; the window does not need rebuilding for it. Keyed by man, then by window, plus `any` for lines that fit any hour. The `game` block is hide and seek, read by the pane only when the game is built into it; it is written here whether or not it is, so that turning the game on is a one-file change to the pane and not a two-file one.

any: There's always food. That isn't luck, it's a policy.
If you're standing there deciding whether to knock, knock.
Bread's proving. Most of the job is waiting and then taking the credit.
I'd offer you something, but you're on the other side of a window.
Somebody left the flour out. It was me. I'm dealing with it.
The kitchen isn't a domain. It's just where the knives live.
morning: Coffee's on. I made too much again, which is the correct amount.
Six in the morning is the only time this kitchen is quiet. I get about forty minutes.
The dough's been up longer than I have. Show off.
Awake since five and I have already lost a spatula.
Moose has decided the morning starts when he says it does. He's usually right.
afternoon: Second lunch is a real meal. I've done the research.
Something's in the oven and I'm pretending to be relaxed about it.
This is the hour where I open the fridge, look in, and close it. Twice.
Afternoons are for the slow things. Stock, bread, and arguments about height.
I'm told the leftovers were for everyone. I'm reviewing that policy.
night: Kitchen's closed. The kitchen is never closed. Ask me anyway.
There's soup. There is always soup at this hour.
Everyone's fed, the counter's clean, and I'm going to sit down for one minute.
This is my favorite hour. Nobody needs anything and I can hear the fridge.
If you're up this late, eat something. That's not advice, that's the rule here.
spring: The window is open for the first time this year. I keep putting a jumper on anyway.
Everything smells green. I have started putting herbs in things that do not need herbs.
Petals all over the sill. I am not sweeping them up yet.
summer: Too hot to have the oven on, so obviously I have had the oven on.
The light goes on forever this time of year. Dinner keeps happening at ten.
There are things on the roof that want watering and I am pretending not to notice the time.
autumn: Soup weather. I have been waiting for soup weather since about March.
The leaves get in whenever anybody opens the door. I have stopped minding.
First proper cold day, and the oven has been on since noon for no particular reason.
winter: It is warm in here and it is not warm out there, and that is most of what a kitchen is for.
Snow. I have been out in it once already and I will go again.
Everything takes twice as long to rise in this cold. Worth it.

any: You are looking at a picture of a room. I am aware of the irony.
Everything here is where I put it. That is the entire decor.
People assume the glasses are prescription. I let them.
I do not tidy. I place a thing once.
The shelves are ordered. Not alphabetically. Better than alphabetically.
I am told a window ought to be inviting. I have decided that is optional.
morning: I have been awake for some time. That is not an accusation.
The morning is the only part of the day nobody has interfered with yet.
Somebody has moved the kettle. I will work out who, and I will say nothing.
I do not require conversation before eight. I am told this is noticeable.
The light is correct at this hour. The rest of the day is a compromise.
afternoon: Yes, I am reading. No, it is not urgent. That is rather the point of it.
The afternoon is when people schedule things. I have views about people.
I am working. The stillness is the work. This is not obvious from outside.
Someone downstairs is being cheerful at volume. I am choosing to allow it.
I have been in this chair two hours and moved once, deliberately.
night: The house is quiet and everything is where I left it. A good night.
I keep late hours. It is preference, not insomnia, and I will not be examined on it.
There is tea going cold beside me. There is always tea going cold beside me.
At this hour the only sound is the building. I find that acceptable.
I am told the correct thing to do now is sleep. I have noted the advice.
spring: The light has moved forty minutes earlier in a fortnight. I noticed on the third day.
Everything out there is putting out growth it cannot yet support. It is a strategy.
Petals get into the hinges, and nobody thinks about it until the door sticks.
summer: The long evenings are useful. Nothing closes when it says it will.
Fireflies, if you are up late enough. They are not signalling to you.
Heat makes people careless about what they say. I find the season informative.
autumn: Everything is dropping what it cannot carry through the cold. I will not spell out the rest.
The leaves go to the same corner of the yard every year. The wind is not improvising.
Better light for reading, and less of it. An awkward trade.
winter: Sound carries differently in cold air. You can hear the quay from here tonight.
Snow records everything that walks through it. I approve of the principle.
Short days. The work does not get shorter.

any: A bed should outlast the building it is in. That is the whole of my opinion on furniture.
Water first, then hands. It is a good order for a day.
The garden is slower than anyone wants. That is not a fault in the garden.
I do not rate a loaf on the day it is baked. Come back on the fifth.
There is a piece of wood in my room that holds nothing up. I kept it anyway.
You are welcome to stand there a while. Nothing here is in a hurry.
morning: The day is long and it has only just started. There is no need to run at it.
I am up before the light most days. The light does not seem to mind.
I have made tea. It will be too hot for eleven minutes. I have waited longer for less.
Something in the garden grew overnight. It does that whether I watch or not.
Mornings are honest. Nothing has gone wrong yet and nobody is pretending it has.
afternoon: This is the hour the day leans on. Everything after it is easier.
I am doing one thing slowly. It will be finished when it is finished.
The wood was cut before I was born. I am only the second person to have a view about it.
Somebody upstairs is arguing about an inch. It has been going on for a year.
Sunday's bread is better today. I said it would be. Nobody has come back to confirm it.
night: The house settles at night. So does everyone in it, eventually.
I do not need much sleep. I have never worked out whether that is a gift.
It is late and the kitchen light is on. It usually is.
This is a good hour for a long thought. There is nowhere for it to be interrupted.
Everything here will outlast the week. That is a comfortable thing to sit with.
spring: Ground is soft again. Good time to put something in it.
It comes back every year. That is the whole trick of it.
Everything young out there. It does not know yet how hard it gets.
summer: Warm enough to sit out. I do.
The heat will break. It always does.
autumn: Good season. It asks you to finish what you started.
The cold is coming, and it is not a threat. It is a date.
winter: Nothing to do out there now but wait, and waiting is a job.
Snow. It will be gone, and it will be back.

julian: Right. I am somewhere. For the record, I did try.
Hidden. I will say now that this was the only room I fit in.
Go on. I am going to be very still and it is not going to help.
vex: I am concealed. You will not find me quickly.
Hidden, on sightlines rather than sentiment.
Begin. I would like to watch your method.
alaric: I am hidden. Take your time.
Go on. I am not going anywhere.

julian: Warmer. Sorry. I cannot help myself.
Warm. That was me helping, which is cheating, and I am at peace with it.
Close. Very close. I am saying nothing else.
vex: Closer. I will not say by how much.
You are warm, and that was not a guess. We both know it.
Warmer. Do it again and think about why it worked.

julian: Colder. Lovely room though.
Not there. Never been in there in my life.
Cold. Keep going, you are doing well.
vex: No.
Cold. You are searching where you would hide, which is a different problem.
Not there. That room has one door and I do not use rooms with one door.

julian: How. I was so still.
Found. I have a great many limbs and they all had to go somewhere.
Fair. Six foot five and a curtain was never going to work.
Right, yes. I was going to come out anyway. Eventually. Probably.
Well spotted. I was holding my breath and I want you to know it did nothing.
You got me. I knocked something over a minute ago and chose not to mention it.
Ah. I did wonder whether the shoes were visible.
Found. In my defence, this was the only room with a door I fit through.
There you are. I was starting to talk to myself in here.
Yes. Alright. I am not built for this and we both knew that going in.
vex: You were guessing. I would like that noted.
Found. Your third choice did the work, not your first.
Acceptable. Ask me again in an hour and it will be harder.
Correct. I will not tell you which part of that was skill.
Yes. You went to the room with two exits, which is the right instinct applied badly.
Found. I assumed you would start where you started. You did not. Noted.
Well. A better result than the method deserved.
You have me. I would like to watch you repeat it.
Correct, and slower than you think. I counted.
Found. I chose this room for the sightline, and nobody was looking down it.
alaric: You looked properly. That is the whole of it.
Found. Seven feet was always going to be a problem.
Good. You did not rush it.
Yes. I heard you two rooms ago.
Found. I was not going to move.
You had it narrowed before you opened the door.

julian: That was immediate. That was genuinely insulting.
One look? I had a whole plan.
Straight here. Lovely. I will be reconsidering everything.
vex: That fast. Either you know something or you were lucky, and I dislike both.
Two looks. I will be revising my assumptions.
Immediately. I would very much like to know why.

julian: Finally. My leg went to sleep about four rooms ago.
There you are. I have had time to think about a great many things.
Took you a while. I am not complaining, I am noting it, warmly.
vex: At last. I had begun composing a list of the things you were doing wrong.
You took your time. I have been standing still and thinking about doors.
Found, eventually. I want the number recorded.
alaric: You kept going. That is the part worth having.
A long look. It did not put you off.
There. You did not give up.

julian: It is my room. I was always going to end up in my room.
Yes, I hid in my own bedroom. I have had a lot on today.
vex: My own room. I am aware of how that reads.
Here. The room I know best, which is either the worst hiding place or the only one.
alaric: My room. It has the fewest corners.
Here. I did not think you would try it first.

nobody: The Room is empty just now, so there is nobody in the flat to go and hide.
Nobody is home to hide. Come back when somebody is in.
